introduction:
# Current Calor language reference

This reference describes the current compiler, not a final 0.30 grammar or a measured token budget.
Write `.calr` files. Bodies are indented two spaces and structural blocks end at dedent.
Source declarations carry no IDs; tooling keeps declaration identity in `.calor/ids.json`. Use tooling for renames.
Use inline signatures, name-first bindings, and indented conditional branches.
Use `§C{target} §A arg §/C` for calls, including nested calls inside prefix expressions.
Use nullable .NET types (`?str`, `?i32`, `null`) and exceptions for absence and failure.
Do not handwrite raw C# passthrough. Conversion fallback capabilities belong in `calor_help action=features`.
Arrays and collections are different: `File.ReadAllLines` returns `[str]`, not `List<str>`.
Contracts evaluate in order: check for null before reading length or members.
Use only supported arguments for built-ins; `(indexof text value :ordinal)` selects ordinal comparison.
Single quotes produce characters; double quotes produce strings.

Query a specific feature with `calor_help` for detailed syntax and examples.
overview:
## Calor Language Overview

Module and function bodies use indentation. Control Flow uses indented branches and loops.
Contracts and Effects describe obligations and side effects. Async functions use `§AF` and `§AWAIT`.
Collections use ordinary .NET types; Typed Literals include `INT:42`, `STR:"hello"`, and `BOOL:true`.
Property and Indexer declarations use `§PROP` and `§IXER`.
Query a specific feature for complete examples; use `action=features` for conversion support.
agentInstructions:
Calor is an indentation-only DSL that compiles to C# on .NET 10.

### MANDATORY Rules for AI Agents

Rule 0: Read `calor://primer` once before writing Calor. Use `calor_help` with `query` or `feature` for details; `action=features` reports conversion capabilities.
Rule 1: Never create new `.cs` files. All new code MUST be written in Calor; new files must be `.calr` files.
Rule 2: Convert C# to Calor before modifying: use `calor_convert`, then edit the `.calr` source. Use `calor analyze` for migration assessment.
Rule 3: Never edit generated files (`.g.cs`).
Rule 4: Compile after writing with `calor_compile` (autoFix is on by default); apply diagnostics and verify contracts with `calor_verify`.

Indent bodies two spaces. Structural blocks end at dedent. Bindings put the name before the type; prefix mutable names with `~`. Use indented conditional branches and inline function signatures. Expressions use prefix notation; section expressions can nest inside them. Use nullable .NET types and exceptions for absence and failure. Do not handwrite raw C# passthrough; the converter owns fallback output.

Read `calor://effects` for effect codes, `calor://tags` for syntax, `calor://id-prefixes` for tooling-owned identity, and `calor://workflows` for editing workflows. Use `calor_file_write` for atomic checked edits; for multi-file edits use `calor_session_open` and `calor_session_close`.

These are best-effort agent instructions; compiler diagnostics remain authoritative.

Convert before modifying existing C#. Agent hooks are best-effort; repository CI is the backstop for changes against a protected base.

constructs.description: Creates a new instance of a class. The class name goes in braces; constructor arguments use §A. Use §NEW{ClassName} §/NEW for zero-argument constructors.
Declares a variable binding. Use ~ prefix for mutable variables. Immutable by default. Give null an explicit existing nullable type, such as ?str.
Defines a method within a class. Supports visibility (pub/priv/prot) and modifiers such as virt/vr, over/ov, abs, stat/st, and seal.
Defines a standalone function (not a class member). Use for top-level functions or static utility methods.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public static int Add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }
private void Log(string message) { Console.WriteLine(message); }

constructs.description: Creates an anonymous function using name:type parameter pairs. It can capture variables from its enclosing scope. The closing delimiter carries no source ID. Bind local helpers as lambdas, not nested §F declarations. Automatic local-function conversion only lowers noncapturing, non-generic direct same-point calls with ordinary parameters; unsupported cases remain explicit converter preservation.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x => x * 2
(a, b) => a + b
items.Where(x => x > 5)

constructs.description: Defines a property with optional getter and setter. Auto-properties use accessor shorthand such as get,set, get,priset, or get,init. Full properties use indented §GET and §SET bodies.
Defines an indexer on a class or interface. Full indexers use indented §I parameters and §GET/§SET/§INIT bodies. Compact auto-indexers use accessor shorthand and inline parameters.

constructs.calorSyntax: Property: use bare member expression (e.g., obj.Property). Method: use §C{obj.Method} args.
constructs.description: §C{...} emits parentheses, making it a method call. For property or field access (no parentheses), use a bare dotted expression in a binding (§B{var} obj.Property) or directly as an expression. Do NOT use §C for property access — it will emit obj.Property() with unwanted parens.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var items = Data.Products;
var items = Data.GetProducts();

constructs.description: For loop with an inclusive integer range. The body is indented under the loop header.
Iterates a collection with an indented body.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
foreach (var item in items) { ... }
foreach (var (key, value) in dictionary) { ... }

constructs.description: Executes body while condition is true.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
while (count > 0) { count--; }
while (true) { if (done) break; }

constructs.description: Conditional branching. §EI for else-if, §EL for else. Both are optional.
Conditional expression (ternary operator). Uses prefix notation with (? ...) syntax. Both branches are expressions, not statements.
Returns a value from a function or method. Use bare §R for void returns.
Defines a class. Supports modifiers such as abs, seal, partial, stat, struct, and readonly. Use §EXT for base class and §IMPL for interfaces.
Defines an async function. Use §AF for standalone async functions, §AMT for async class methods.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public async Task<string> FetchDataAsync() { ... }
public async Task ProcessAsync() { await DoWork(); }

constructs.description: Awaits an asynchronous operation.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var result = await FetchAsync();
await Task.Delay(1000);

constructs.description: Exception handling. §TR for try block, §CA for catch (with optional type and variable), §FI for finally.
Throws an exception. Use §RT to rethrow in a catch block.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
throw new ArgumentException("Invalid");
throw;

constructs.description: Declares side effects a function may have. Common effects: cw (console write), db (database), net (network), fs:r/fs:w (file system), rand (random), time, and env. Unresolved external effects are not purity proofs; supply authoritative effect metadata rather than inventing an effect code.
Declares a precondition that must be true when the function is called. Part of Design by Contract.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Contract.Requires(value >= 0)
// Guard.Against.Null(input)

constructs.description: Declares a postcondition that will be true when the function returns. Use result to refer to the return value.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Contract.Ensures(result >= 0)
// Ensures non-empty result

constructs.description: Declares an invariant at module scope.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // [ContractInvariantMethod] void Invariants() { Contract.Invariant(_count >= 0); }

constructs.description: Calls a method or function. Each argument uses §A; §/C delimits nested argument lists.
Defines a field in a class. Usually private, prefixed with underscore by convention.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
private string _name;
private readonly int _id;

constructs.description: Defines an interface with method signatures.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public interface IRepository { void Save(Entity e); }

constructs.description: Defines an enumeration. Enum values are indented under §EN and may use = for explicit values.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public enum Status { Active, Inactive, Pending }
public enum Priority : byte { Low = 0, High = 1 }

constructs.description: Defines a class constructor. Use §BASE with §A arguments to call a base constructor, or §THIS to chain constructors.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public User(string name) { _name = name; }
public Admin(string name) : base(name) { }

constructs.calorSyntax: §W expression with indented §K pattern → result cases; use in an expression context, such as §R §W
constructs.description: Pattern matching switch expression. §K introduces each case/pattern. Use _ for default.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x switch { 1 => "one", 2 => "two", _ => "other" }
shape switch { Circle c => c.Area(), Rectangle r => r.Width * r.Height }

constructs.calorSyntax: (?? left right) for null-coalescing, (?. target Member) for null-conditional
constructs.description: Handles nullable values. (?? left right) returns left if non-null, else right. (?. target Member) accesses Member on target only if non-null. Both use Lisp-style prefix notation inside parentheses.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
name ?? "default"
user?.Name
GetValue() ?? fallback

constructs.description: Resource management with automatic disposal.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
using (var stream = File.OpenRead(path)) { ... }
using var connection = new SqlConnection(connStr);

constructs.description: Generic type parameters and constraints.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public class Repository<T> where T : class { }
public T Get<T>(int id) where T : new() { }

constructs.description: LINQ queries use method-chain syntax with §C (call) and §LAM (lambda) in Calor. Complex chains are commonly hoisted into bindings before the final call.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
items.Where(x => x > 5).Select(x => x * 2)
from item in items where item.Active select item.Name

constructs.description: String interpolation uses ${} inside ordinary string literals. Note: ${0}, ${1} etc. are treated as format placeholders, not interpolation.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
$"Hello, {name}!"
$"Total: {price:C2}"
$"{firstName} {lastName}"
$"Result: {Calculate(x, y)} units"

constructs.description: Loop control statements.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
if (done) break;
if (skip) continue;

constructs.description: Query calor_help action=features for record conversion support. Do not handwrite passthrough.

Creates and initializes a fixed-size array. The element type is specified in the header. Elements are space-separated between the opening and closing tags. Supports both explicit (new int[] { ... }) and bare ({ ... }) initializer syntax.
Defines a named module for static members. Its functions use §F; C# callers keep the original static class name. Static class declarations with §CL are rejected.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public static class StringHelper { }

constructs.description: Defines a virtual method that can be overridden in derived classes. Use the 'virt' modifier (the compiler also accepts 'vr').
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public virtual string GetName() { return _name; }
protected virtual void OnChanged() { }

constructs.description: Overrides a virtual method from a base class. Use the 'over' modifier (the compiler also accepts 'ov').
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public override string ToString() { return _name; }
public override int GetHashCode() { return _id; }

constructs.description: Defines an abstract class that cannot be instantiated directly. Use 'abs' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public abstract class Shape { }

constructs.description: Defines an abstract method with no body that must be overridden. Use 'abs' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public abstract double GetArea();

constructs.description: Defines a sealed class that cannot be inherited from. Use 'seal' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public sealed class FinalClass { }

constructs.description: Locks an object while executing the indented body.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: lock (_sync) { _count++; }

constructs.description: Use ordinary comments for todo items, fixmes and hacks.
Marks code as deprecated with a reason.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: [Obsolete("Use NewMethod instead")]

constructs.description: Document algorithmic complexity in an ordinary comment.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
// Complexity: O(n log n)
// Complexity: O(1) - constant time

constructs.description: Visibility modifiers are specified in the tag header. Use 'pub' for public, 'priv' for private, 'prot' for protected.
Defines an event. Simple form has no body. For custom add/remove accessors, use indented §EADD and §EREM blocks inside the event body.
Defines an operator overload for a class or struct. Supports binary operators (+, -, *, /, ==, etc.), unary operators (-, !, ~, ++, --), and conversion operators (implicit, explicit).

constructs.calorSyntax: DECIMAL:value or DEC:value or value with m/M suffix
constructs.description: Decimal literals for precise numeric values. Use DECIMAL: or DEC: prefix, or append m/M suffix.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
decimal price = 18.0000m;
decimal total = 100m;

constructs.description: Single Unicode character. Uses 'char' type name directly (no abbreviation).
constructs.csharpEquivalent: char c = 'A';

constructs.description: Produces values lazily from an iterator method. §YIELD returns a value, §YBRK stops iteration.

constructs.calorSyntax: §DEL{name} with indented §I parameters and optional §O return type
constructs.description: Defines a delegate type (function signature). Use for callbacks, event handlers, and function references. §DEL can appear at the top level or nested inside §CL class bodies.

Conditional compilation blocks use §PP for #if and §PPE for #else. Indented statement bodies end at dedent. Nested §PP blocks express #elif. Code inside is conditionally included based on defined symbols.
Defines a value type (struct). Uses the 'struct' modifier on §CL. Supports readonly structs with the 'readonly' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
public struct Point { public int X; public int Y; }
public readonly struct Vector2D { public readonly double X; public readonly double Y; }

constructs.description: Constrains generic type parameters. Supports class, struct, new(), interface, and base class constraints.
Runs the indented body at least once; the matching closer carries the condition.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: do { Process(); } while (HasMore());

constructs.description: Defines part of a class that can be split across multiple files. Uses the 'partial' modifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: public partial class UserService { public void Save() { } }

constructs.description: Marks a block for unsafe pointer operations. Required for pointer arithmetic, fixed statements, and stackalloc.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: unsafe { int* ptr = &value; *ptr = 42; }

constructs.calorSyntax: §IF (== x null) with indented §ASSIGN x default
constructs.description: C#'s ??= operator has no direct Calor equivalent. Use an §IF null check with §ASSIGN as a workaround.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
x ??= GetDefault();
_cache ??= new Dictionary<string, int>();

constructs.calorSyntax: Attach [@AttributeName] or [@Attr(arg1, arg2)] after a declaration header
constructs.description: Attaches metadata to declarations. Placed before the declaration they annotate.
C# 'is' patterns with and/or/not combinators are decomposed into standard boolean expressions using prefix notation. No special tag needed — fully supported natively.
C# range expressions (start..end) and index-from-end (^n) have native Calor forms. Use §RANGE for slicing and §^ for indexing from the end.

constructs.calorSyntax: Supported in C# → Calor migration. Decompose to §IF chains for hand-written Calor.
constructs.description: During C# → Calor migration, positional patterns (tuple deconstruction) and property patterns stay inline. For hand-written Calor, decompose complex patterns into §IF/§EI chains with explicit comparisons.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
(hour, minute) switch { (0, 0) => "midnight" }
obj switch { { Length: > 0 } => true }

constructs.description: Pragma directives use explicit source-ordered conversion nodes. Query calor_help action=features for current support; do not handwrite passthrough.

constructs.calorSyntax: (Type1, Type2) for types; (expr1, expr2) for literals
constructs.description: Tuple types use parenthesized comma-separated types: (i32, str). Tuple literals use parenthesized comma-separated expressions: (1, "hello"). Named tuple elements are supported: (i32 X, i32 Y). Tuples are distinguished from Lisp expressions by the presence of commas.
Null-coalescing operator in Lisp-style prefix notation. Returns left if non-null, otherwise returns right. Use inside parentheses: (?? expr default).
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var result = value ?? "default";
return name ?? "Anonymous";

constructs.description: Null-conditional member access in Lisp-style prefix notation. Accesses MemberName on target only if target is non-null, otherwise returns null. The member name is an unquoted identifier.
constructs.csharpEquivalent:
var name = user?.Name;
var len = text?.Length;

constructs.description: Jump to a specific case label or to the default case in a switch statement. For regular goto, use §GOTO{labelName}.

constructs.calorSyntax: (concat a b), (substr text start count), (indexof text value :ordinal)
constructs.description: Prefix operations include (str value), (concat a b), (fmt "{0}" value), (len text), (contains text value), (starts text prefix), (ends text suffix), (equals left right), (isempty text), (upper text), (lower text), (trim text), (replace text old new) and (substr text start count). indexof accepts an optional start and count; use :ordinal for ordinal comparison. Do not invent extra arguments.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: string.Concat(a, b); text.Substring(start, count); text.IndexOf(value, StringComparison.Ordinal);

constructs.description: Single quotes produce char literals with C# escapes. Built-ins include char-at, char-code, char-from-code, char-upper, char-lower, is-letter, is-digit, is-whitespace, is-upper and is-lower. Character subtraction promotes to i32.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: text[index]; (int)value; char.IsDigit(value);

constructs.description: Use [T] for array types and [[T]] for jagged arrays. Section expressions can nest inside prefix expressions. File.ReadAllLines returns [str], not List<str>.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: array[index]

constructs.description: Declare a mutable binding with a ~-prefixed name; use §ASSIGN for all updates, including increments and compound arithmetic.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: name = expression;

constructs.calorSyntax: i32, i64, i16, u8, u16, u32, u64, f32, f64, dec, str, bool, char, object, void, ?T, [T]
constructs.description: Use the C# type mappings for aliases, ordinary .NET generic types for collections, ?T and null for nullable values. Typed numeric bounds such as INT:-2147483648 avoid an out-of-range positive intermediate. Use double quotes for strings.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: int, long, short, byte, ushort, uint, ulong, float, double, decimal, string, bool, char, object, void, T?, T[]

constructs.calorSyntax: (+ a b), (== a b), (&& a b), (? condition thenValue elseValue)
constructs.description: Arithmetic and comparisons use prefix notation. Boolean operators && and || short circuit; ! negates. Use (- 0 value) for negation and (? condition thenValue elseValue) for a conditional value. Call Math methods for operations not provided as built-ins; method names are not prefix operators.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: a + b; a == b; a && b; condition ? thenValue : elseValue;

constructs.calorSyntax: (forall ((i i32)) body), (exists ((i i32)) body), (-> condition consequence)
constructs.description: Quantifiers declare typed bound variables. Bound runtime quantifiers with finite array ranges; check array lengths against external bounds. Use -> for implication. Contracts are obligations, not a guarantee that every proof succeeds.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: // Universal/existential contracts with bounded ranges.

constructs.description: Ordinary List<T>, Dictionary<K,V> and HashSet<T> are distinct from arrays. Mutating heap collections requires mut; significant allocation requires alloc. §CNT reads count; §HAS tests membership. Use the complete examples for empty construction and iteration.
constructs.csharpEquivalent: list.Add(value); dictionary[key] = value;

§I.name: Input Parameter
§I.syntax: Inline (type:name) parameters in function headers; indented §I{type:name} for delegates and full indexers
§I.description: Header parameter syntax. Modifiers: 'this' (extension method), 'ref', 'out', 'in', 'params'. Default values use =expr in the signature.
§I.csharpEquivalent: Type name, this Type name, ref Type name, params Type[] name, Type name = default

examples.name: Extension Method Parameter
examples.description: Marks this as an extension method parameter (C# 'this' modifier)

§O.name: Output Type
§O.syntax: Inline -> type in function headers; indented §O{type} for delegates
§O.description: Declares the return type of a function or method via the header arrow.

§EXT.name: Extends
§EXT.description: Specifies the base class for inheritance.

§IMPL.name: Implements
§IMPL.description: Specifies an interface the class implements.

§CA.name: Catch Block
§CA.description: Catches exceptions. Type and variable name are optional.

§SET.name: Setter
§SET.description: Property setter with optional visibility modifier.
§SET.csharpEquivalent: set { body } or private set { body }

§THIS.name: This Constructor
§THIS.description: Chains to another constructor in the same class.

§EADD.name: Event Add Accessor
§EADD.description: Custom add accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is subscribed.

§EREM.name: Event Remove Accessor
§EREM.description: Custom remove accessor body inside an event definition (§EVT). Contains statements executed when a handler is unsubscribed.

§K.name: Case
§K.description: A case in a switch expression. Use _ for default.

§WHERE.name: Generic Constraint
§WHERE.description: Constraint on a generic type parameter.

§??.name: Null-Coalescing (Legacy)
§??.description: Legacy null-coalescing syntax. Prefer Lisp-style (?? left right) for null-coalescing.

§?..name: Null-Conditional Access
§?..description: Null-conditional member access in Lisp prefix notation. Returns null if target is null, otherwise accesses Member.

§INTERP.name: String Interpolation
§INTERP.description: Builds an interpolated string from literal parts and §EXP expression parts. Strings are opaque — expressions cannot be embedded inside quotes. Use separate "literal" and §EXP expr parts.

§U.name: Using Import
§U.description: Imports a namespace or creates an alias. Must appear inside a module (§M{Name}) block.
§U.csharpEquivalent: using Namespace; or using Alias = Namespace;

§LIST.name: List
§LIST.csharpEquivalent: new List<Type>() or new List<Type> { elements }

§P.name: Print
§P.description: Prints to console with newline. Use §Pf for no newline.

§EACH.name: Foreach
§EACH.description: Iterates over each element in a collection. Type is inferred in §EACH{variable}; §EACH{variable:type} specifies it explicitly. An optional third field names the index.

§RT.name: Rethrow
§RT.description: Rethrows the current exception in a catch block.

§VAR.name: Variable Pattern
§VAR.description: Captures a value into a variable in pattern matching.

§WHEN.name: Guard Clause
§WHEN.description: Adds a guard condition to a pattern match case.

§A.name: Argument
§A.description: Marks an argument in inline calls or constructors.

§EX.name: Example
§EX.description: Inline example or test code in documentation.

§SN.name: Since
§SN.description: Documents the version when a feature was introduced.

§BR.name: Breaking Change
§BR.description: Documents a breaking change in the API.

§AS.name: Assume
§AS.description: Documents an assumption that must be true at this point in the code.

§EEXT.name: Enum Extension
§EEXT.description: Defines extension methods for an enum type.

§RANGE.name: Range
§RANGE.description: Represents a range value (start..end) for array/span slicing.

§^.name: Index From End
§^.description: Indexes from the end of a collection. Equivalent to C#'s ^n operator.

programs.title: Collection allocation, loop mutation and count
SafeDivide
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference8}
  §F{SafeDivide:pub} (i32:a, i32:b) -> i32
    §E{alloc,throw}
    §IF (!= b 0)
      §R (/ a b)
    §EL
      §TH §NEW{ArgumentException} §A "Division by zero" §/NEW

programs.title: Max
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference10}
  §F{Max:pub} (i32:a, i32:b) -> i32
    §IF (>= a b)
      §R a
    §EL
      §R b

programs.title: GetGrade
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference11}
  §F{GetGrade:pub} (i32:score) -> str
    §B{~grade:str} "F"
    §IF (>= score 90)
      §ASSIGN grade "A"
    §EI (>= score 80)
      §ASSIGN grade "B"
    §EI (>= score 70)
      §ASSIGN grade "C"
    §EL
      §ASSIGN grade "F"
    §R grade

programs.title: DoWhileDemo
SumList
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference14}
  §F{SumList:pub} () -> i32
    §E{alloc,mut}
    §B{nums:List<i32>} §NEW{List<i32>}
    §PUSH{nums} 10
    §PUSH{nums} 20
    §PUSH{nums} 30
    §B{~sum:i32} 0
    §EACH{n} nums
      §ASSIGN sum (+ sum n)
    §R sum

programs.title: IsSingleDigit
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference22}
  §F{IsSingleDigit:pub} (i32:n) -> bool
    §R §W n
      §K 0 → true
      §K 1 → true
      §K 2 → true
      §K 3 → true
      §K 4 → true
      §K 5 → true
      §K 6 → true
      §K 7 → true
      §K 8 → true
      §K 9 → true
      §K _ → false

programs.title: Accumulate
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference27}
  §F{Accumulate:pub} (i32:n) -> i32
    §B{~acc:i32} 0          // Bind mutable variable acc = 0
    §ASSIGN acc (+ acc n)   // Assign acc = acc + n
    §ASSIGN acc (+ acc n)   // Assign again
    §ASSIGN acc (+ acc n)   // And again
    §R acc

programs.title: AbsoluteValue
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference34}
  §F{AbsoluteValue:pub} (i32:x) -> i32
    §S (>= result 0)
    §S (-> (>= x 0) (== result x))
    §S (-> (< x 0) (== result (- 0 x)))
    §R (? (< x 0) (- 0 x) x)

programs.title: BuildGreeting
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference38}
  §F{BuildGreeting:pub} (str:name) -> str
    §E{alloc,mut}
    §B{sb:StringBuilder} (sb-new)
    (sb-append sb "Hello, ")
    (sb-append sb name)
    (sb-append sb "!")
    §R (sb-tostring sb)

programs.title: AllPositive
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference39}
  §F{AllPositive:pub} ([i32]:arr, i32:n) -> bool
    §Q (== n (len arr))
    §S (-> result (forall ((i i32)) (-> (&& (>= i 0) (< i n)) (> arr{i} 0))))
    §B{~allPos:bool} true
    §L{i:0:(- (len arr) 1):1}
      §IF (<= arr{i} 0)
        §ASSIGN allPos false
    §R allPos

programs.title: HasNegative
programs.calor:
§M{AgentReference40}
  §F{HasNegative:pub} ([i32]:arr, i32:n) -> bool
    §Q (== n (len arr))
    §S (== result (exists ((i i32)) (&& (&& (>= i 0) (< i n)) (< arr{i} 0))))
    §L{i:0:(- (len arr) 1):1}
      §IF (< arr{i} 0)
        §R true
    §R false

programs.title: Contracts
programs.calor:
§M{Contracts}
  §F{Square:pub} (i32:x) -> i32
    §Q (>= x 0)
    §S (>= result 0)
    §R (* x x)

  §F{Divide:pub} (i32:a, i32:b) -> i32
    §Q{"divisor must not be zero"} (!= b 0)
    §R (/ a b)

programs.title: Files
programs.calor:
§M{Files}
  §F{Append:pub} (str:path, str:key, str:value) -> void
    §E{fs:w}
    §C{File.AppendAllText} §A path §A (+ key (+ "=" (+ value "\n"))) §/C

  §F{CountLines:pub} (str:path) -> i32
    §E{fs:r}
    §B{ok:bool} §C{File.Exists} §A path §/C
    §IF (! ok)
      §R 0
    §B{lines:[str]} §C{File.ReadAllLines} §A path §/C
    §R (len lines)

programs.calor:
§M{Strings}
  §F{FirstField:pub} (str:line) -> str
    §E{}
    §B{i:i32} (indexof line "," :ordinal)
    §IF (< i 0)
      §R line
    §R (substr line 0 i)

§M{PointModule}
  §CL{Point:pub}
    §FLD{i32:_x:priv}
    §FLD{i32:_y:priv}

    §CTOR{pub} (i32:x, i32:y)
      §ASSIGN §THIS._x x
      §ASSIGN §THIS._y y

    §MT{Equals:pub} (Point:other) -> bool
      §IF (== other null)
        §R false
      §EL
        §R true

    §OP{==:pub} (Point:left, Point:right) -> bool
      §IF (== left null)
        §R (== right null)
      §EL
        §R §C{left.Equals} §A right §/C

    §OP{!=:pub} (Point:left, Point:right) -> bool
      §R (! (== left right))

§M{LoopControl}
  §F{FirstPositive:pub} ([i32]:values) -> i32
    §E{}
    §B{~answer:i32} 0
    §EACH{value:i32} values

    §R answer

primer.introduction:
# Calor syntax exemplar (reference sheet)

Calor is an indentation-only DSL (2 spaces per level, Python-style) that compiles
<!-- drift:ignore -->
to C#. **Never write structural closer tags** (`§/M`, `§/F`, `§/IF`, `§/WH`,
`§/EACH`, ... are hard errors); blocks end by dedent. Value delimiters remain where documented: calls (`§/C`), block lambdas
(`§/LAM`), constructors (`§/NEW`), empty collection literals, and the do-while
condition carried by `§/DO`. Structural blocks end at dedent.

Every complete `§M{...}` program in the "Complete programs" section below compiles
(the compiler's own tests prove it); the reference blocks show the shape of each
construct, and every idiom in them is exercised by one of those programs.

## Core tags

```
§M{Name}                     Module
§F{Name:pub} (str:x) -> str  Function, inline signature (priv = private)
§E{}                            Effects: §E{} pure; fs:r, fs:w, fs:rw file I/O;
                                mut collection/heap mutation; cw console; comma-join
§B{name:str} expr               Immutable binding (type annotation optional: §B{name})
§B{~name:i32} 0                 Mutable binding (~ prefix required to reassign)
§ASSIGN name expr               Reassign a mutable binding
§Q (pre)  §S (post)             Precondition / postcondition (post can use `result`)
§R expr                         Return (bare §R for void)
§P expr                         Print line
§IF (cond) / §EI (cond) / §EL   If / else-if / else (§EI/§EL at §IF's column)
§WH (cond)                  While loop
§L{i:0:9:1}                  For loop, i from 0 to 9 step 1 (inclusive)
§EACH{x} coll                Foreach over list/array
§EACHKV{k:v} dict            Foreach over dictionary
```

Expressions are prefix s-expressions: `(+ a b)`, `(== a b)`, `(&& p q)`, `(! p)`,
`(< i n)`, `(% n 3)`. String `+` concatenates. Typed literals when needed:
`INT:42`, `STR:"hi"`, `BOOL:true`. Escapes in strings: `\"`, `\n`, `\r`.

## Calls

```
§C{Obj.Method} §A arg1 §A arg2 §/C     each arg prefixed §A, closed with §/C
§B{lines:[str]} §C{File.ReadAllLines} §A path §/C
§C{File.AppendAllText} §A path §A (+ key (+ "=" (+ value "\n"))) §/C
§B{ok:bool} §C{File.Exists} §A path §/C
§B{n:i32} §C{LocalFunc} §A x §/C       user functions are called the same way
```

## Strings (prefix ops, not method calls)

```
(len s)                 s.Length            (substr s start count)   s.Substring
(contains s sub)        s.Contains          (indexof s sub :ordinal) s.IndexOf
(starts s pre)          s.StartsWith        (replace s old new)      s.Replace
(trim s)  (upper s)  (lower s)  (equals a b)  (ends s suf)
§B{c:str} (substr line i 1)      // single char at i, as a str
```

## Lists and dictionaries

```
§LIST{items:str}          empty list literal — close the empty form with §/LIST
§/LIST
§PUSH{items} x            items.Add(x)         [needs mut effect]
§B{n:i32} §CNT{items}     items.Count
§B{e:str} §IDX items i    items[i]
§IF (! §HAS{items} k)   Contains check (dict key: §HAS{d} §KEY k)
§DICT{ages:str:i32}       empty dict literal
§/DICT
§PUT{ages} k v            ages[k] = v          [needs mut effect]
```

A function whose body mutates a collection (`§PUSH`, `§PUT`, `§SETIDX`) must
declare `mut` in `§E{...}`; file reads/writes need `fs:r` / `fs:w` / `fs:rw`.
Callers must declare (at least) the union of their callees' effects.

**Arrays vs lists (common trap):** `File.ReadAllLines` returns an ARRAY — bind it
as `[str]`. Do NOT copy `[str]` into signatures that require `List<str>`; match
the type the surrounding surface declares.
primer.mistakes:
## Common mistakes (these do NOT compile — shown so you avoid them)

```
<!-- drift:ignore -->
§/F §/M §/I §/L       removed; use indentation only (a block ends on dedent)
<!-- drift:ignore -->
§S (>= §RESULT 0)     wrong; the return value is lowercase: §S (>= result 0)
§IF                  wrong; §IF needs a condition, such as §IF (> x 0)
§IF{i1}{x > 0}        wrong; the condition goes in (parens), not braces
<!-- drift:ignore -->
§K   §ELSE            no such keywords; else is §EL, else-if is §EI (no id)
§F{f1:Add:i32:pub}    wrong; a 4-field header drops the return type. Use:
                     §F{Add:pub} (i32:a, i32:b) -> i32
```

Effects: `§E{cw}` declares console write; declare effects on any function that
performs I/O. See the `calor://effects` resource for the full effect catalog.

catalogs.type-mappings.md:
# C# → Calor Type Mappings

| C# Type | Calor Type | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------|
| `int` | `i32` | 32-bit signed integer |
| `long` | `i64` | 64-bit signed integer |
| `short` | `i16` | 16-bit signed integer |
| `byte` | `u8` | 8-bit unsigned integer |
| `float` | `f32` | 32-bit floating point |
| `double` | `f64` | 64-bit floating point |
| `decimal` | `dec` | 128-bit decimal |
| `string` | `str` | UTF-16 string |
| `bool` | `bool` | Boolean |
| `char` | `char` | Unicode character |
| `void` | `void` | No return value |
| `object` | `object` | Base type |
| `int?` / `Nullable<int>` | `?i32` | Nullable value |
| `Task<T>` | use `§AF`/`§AMT` | Async function/method |
| `List<T>` | `§LIST{name:type}` | List collection |
| `Dictionary<K,V>` | `§DICT{name:key:val}` | Dictionary collection |
| `HashSet<T>` | `§HSET{name:type}` | HashSet collection |
